subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
options: Nuclear fuel
Wind
Natural gas
Coal
questions.explain: Wind is renewable as it is replenished and will not run out. Coal, natural gas and nuclear fuel are finite (non-renewable) resources.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the difference between energy and power?
options: Power is the rate at which energy is transferred
Energy is measured in watts; power in joules
Energy and power are the same quantity
Power is energy stored; energy is the rate of transfer
questions.explain: Power is the energy transferred per second (P = E/t), measured in watts; energy is measured in joules. Confusing the two is a common error.

questions.q: What happens when an electron in an atom absorbs electromagnetic radiation of the right energy?
options: It turns into a proton
It moves to a higher energy level (further from the nucleus)
It moves to a lower energy level
It leaves the atom and becomes a neutron
questions.explain: Absorbing EM radiation can move an electron to a higher energy level. When it falls back to a lower level it emits EM radiation.

questions.q: What makes a main sequence star (like the Sun) stable for billions of years?
options: It is constantly shrinking
The inward force of gravity is balanced by the outward pressure from fusion energy
There are no forces acting on it
It is held together by magnetism
questions.explain: During the main sequence the inward pull of gravity is balanced by the outward force from the expansion of hot gases (energy released by hydrogen fusion). This equilibrium keeps the star stable.

questions.q: Work is done on an object when a force makes it move. What energy transfer often warms the surroundings when work is done against friction?
options: The force loses its weight
Energy is destroyed by the friction
Energy is created from nothing
Energy is transferred to the thermal store, raising temperature
questions.explain: Work done against friction transfers energy to the thermal store of the object and surroundings, so they warm up. Energy is conserved, not created or destroyed.

questions.q: Heating a substance without changing its state increases its internal energy. Specifically, it increases the particles'...
options: number
mass
potential energy only, so temperature stays constant
kinetic energy, so the temperature rises
questions.explain: When heating raises temperature (no state change), the energy increases the particles' kinetic energy, so they move faster and the temperature rises.

questions.q: A ball is thrown straight up. As it rises (before reaching the top), which energy transfer mainly occurs?
options: Thermal to kinetic
Gravitational potential to kinetic
Kinetic to gravitational potential
Chemical to kinetic
questions.explain: As the ball rises it slows down, so its kinetic store falls while its gravitational potential store rises: energy is transferred from kinetic to gravitational potential.

questions.q: In the specific heat capacity required practical, why is a layer of insulation wrapped around the metal block?
options: To speed up heating
To reduce energy lost to the surroundings
To raise the heater's power
To increase the block's mass
questions.explain: Insulation reduces energy dissipated to the surroundings, so more of the electrical energy supplied raises the block's temperature, giving a more accurate value of c.

questions.q: A child slides down a slide and ends up moving more slowly than a frictionless calculation predicts. Where has the 'missing' energy gone?
options: Converted entirely to sound
It has been destroyed
Stored as extra chemical energy
Dissipated as thermal energy by friction
questions.explain: Energy is conserved and cannot be destroyed. Friction dissipates energy to the thermal store of the slide and surroundings, so less reaches the kinetic store.

questions.q: What is the role of a step-down transformer in the national grid?
options: It decreases the p.d. to a safe value for homes
It increases the current in the transmission cables
It converts ac to dc
It increases the p.d. before transmission
questions.explain: A step-down transformer reduces the high transmission potential difference to a safer, lower value (about 230 V) for use in homes. Step-up transformers raise the p.d. for transmission.

questions.q: What is meant by the internal energy of a system?
options: Only the kinetic energy of the particles
The total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles
The energy supplied by an external heater
Only the potential energy stored between particles
questions.explain: Internal energy is the total energy stored by the particles: the sum of their kinetic energy (from motion) and the potential energy stored in the bonds/forces between them.

questions.q: During the main sequence stage, what process releases energy in a star's core?
options: Nuclear fission of uranium
Burning of fuel like a fire (combustion)
Gravitational collapse only
Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium
questions.explain: Main sequence stars release energy by nuclear fusion, joining hydrogen nuclei to form helium. This is not chemical burning — it is a nuclear process in the core.

questions.q: What happens to the average kinetic energy of gas particles as the temperature of the gas increases?
options: It increases
It stays the same
It decreases
It depends on the container size
questions.explain: The temperature of a gas is related to the average kinetic energy of its particles: raising the temperature increases their average kinetic energy, so they move faster.

questions.q: What is nuclear fusion?
options: A nucleus emitting an alpha particle
Two light nuclei joining to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
An electron joining the nucleus
A large unstable nucleus splitting into two smaller nuclei
questions.explain: Fusion is the joining of two light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy (as in the Sun). Fission is the splitting of a large unstable nucleus into smaller ones.

questions.q: Which particles are found inside the nucleus of an atom?
options: Protons and neutrons
Neutrons and electrons
Protons and electrons
Only electrons
questions.explain: The nucleus contains protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral). Electrons (negative) orbit the nucleus in energy levels (shells).

questions.q: Which method would best reduce unwanted energy transfers between a machine's moving parts?
options: Lubrication
Adding more mass
Painting it black
Increasing the temperature
questions.explain: Lubrication reduces friction between moving parts, reducing energy dissipated to the thermal store. Insulation and streamlining are other valid methods of reducing unwanted transfers.

questions.q: What is the activity of a radioactive source?
options: The energy of each emitted particle
The number of undecayed nuclei remaining
The mass of the source
The rate at which its nuclei decay, measured in becquerel (Bq)
questions.explain: Activity is the rate at which nuclei of a source decay, measured in becquerel (Bq), where 1 Bq is one decay per second.

questions.q: On a force–extension graph, what does the gradient of the straight (linear) region represent?
options: The limit of proportionality
The spring constant
The elastic potential energy
The weight of the spring
questions.explain: For the linear region, F = ke, so the gradient (force ÷ extension) is the spring constant k. The area under the line gives the elastic potential energy stored.

questions.q: A student says 'current is used up as it goes round a series circuit, so the second lamp is dimmer.' Why is this wrong?
options: Current is only in the first half of the circuit
Current is voltage divided by charge
Current is the same everywhere in a series circuit
Current increases round a series circuit
questions.explain: Current is the rate of flow of charge and is the same at every point in a single series loop. Charge (and current) is not 'used up'; energy is transferred from the potential difference.

questions.q: In the national grid, what is the role of a step-down transformer near homes?
options: To increase the current in the transmission lines
To convert ac to dc
To lower the voltage to a safer level for domestic use
To raise the voltage for long-distance transmission
questions.explain: Step-up transformers raise the voltage for efficient transmission; step-down transformers near towns and homes lower the voltage (e.g. to 230 V) so it is safe to use in buildings.

questions.q: What was Bohr's key contribution to the development of the atomic model?
options: He fired alpha particles at gold foil
He proposed the plum pudding model
He discovered the proton
He suggested electrons orbit the nucleus at specific fixed distances (energy levels)
questions.explain: Bohr adapted the nuclear model by proposing that electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances (energy levels), which matched experimental observations.

questions.q: Why does the national grid use step-up transformers before transmission over long distances?
options: To increase the voltage and reduce the current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables
To increase the current and reduce the voltage
To convert ac to dc for transmission
To make the cables thicker
questions.explain: Stepping up the p.d. reduces the current for the same power (P = VI). Lower current means much less energy wasted as heat in the resistance of the transmission cables (heating ∝ I²R).
